title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 1986 first draft of 'Analysis situs'. Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, point-free framework.
- A set M of 'multiplicités' carries a partial order ≤ (inclusion-like) and a second relation ≪ ('is dominated by' / 'is relatively small in'), together with a compatibility relation.
- A figure is a set of multiplicités. Figures have 'ombres' (shadows) and 'lieux' (places, i.e. points). Contrées are regions, i.e. suitable subsets of M.
- On p.38, X and Y are disjoint if they are compatible and no Z in M satisfies Z ≤ X and Z ≤ Y. Two figures are disjoint iff every X in F is disjoint from every Y in G.
- Also on p.38, F refines G iff for every X in F there is Y in G with X ≤ Y (or X ≪ Y for elementary figures).

This page adds two axioms on the structure M.

Cond 5 (added to Cond 2 of p.33): if X and Y are disjoint and X' ≪ X, Y' ≪ Y, then X' and Y' are disjoint. Grothendieck splits this in two:
- (a) X' and Y' are again compatible.
- (b) no Z in M satisfies Z ≪ X and Z ≪ Y.
- Parenthetical: when X and Y are compatible, M_{≤X} ∩ M_{≤Y} = ∅ should also give M_{≪X} ∩ M_{≪Y} = ∅.
- A crossed-out attempt shows he first tried to deduce disjointness directly. From Z ≤ X', Z ≤ Y' he got Z ≪ X and Z ≪ Y, then needed (b) to conclude.

Corollary: disjointness of figures is stable under refinement. If F and G are disjoint, any refinement F' of F and G' of G are disjoint. This follows elementwise from Cond 5.

Remark: for a sub-construction M' ('dirigée multiplicativement' in X, Y), disjointness of figures in M' agrees with disjointness in M, and Cond 5 passes from M to M'. The same holds for Cond 6.

Cond 6 (marked 'facultatif ?'): suppose the shadows (sets of lieux) X̃ and Ỹ are disjoint and every point of X̃ is compatible with every point of Ỹ. Then X and Y are disjoint. Margin note: hence every x in X̃ is disjoint from every y in Ỹ.
- This is an 'enough points' or spatiality axiom: disjointness can be detected on points.
- The analogue in locales: if two opens have no common point, their meet is 0.

Purpose: p.40 defines induced and residual contrées. The residual contrée C_{CF} is the set of X disjoint from F, and its closure under ≪ uses Cond 5.
errors: The parenthetical claim, that M_{≤X} ∩ M_{≤Y} = ∅ implies M_{≪X} ∩ M_{≪Y} = ∅ for compatible X and Y, does not follow from the axioms visible here. One would need 'Z ≪ X and Z compatible with X implies Z ≤ X' (p.38) together with compatibility of Z with X and Y. That compatibility is not given, which is presumably why (b) is stated separately as an axiom.

Refinement is defined with ≤ on p.38 but described with ≪ for elementary figures. The Corollary needs refinement to be compatible with the ≪ in Cond 5, for example via ≤ ∘ ≪ ⊂ ≪ or ≪ ⊂ ≤. This is not stated on the page.

ideas.what: Axiom: disjointness is preserved when both elements are shrunk via ≪ (Cond 5), split into compatibility-preservation and absence of common ≪-lower bounds
ideas.modern_name: stability of disjointness under a way-below-like relation (cf. U' ⋐ U in topology; way-below relation in continuous posets/domains)
ideas.usually_credited_to: way-below relation: Scott (1972), Gierz–Hofmann–Keimel–Lawson–Mislove–Scott, Compendium of Continuous Lattices (1980)

ideas.what: Corollary: disjointness of figures is stable under refinement; inheritance of the conditions by sub-constructions
Cond 6: disjoint shadows (sets of points) plus pointwise compatibility imply disjointness of the multiplicities
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ehresmann, Bénabou, Isbell (1972), Johnstone, Stone Spaces (1982)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics for 'multiplicités' with ≤, ≪, compatibility and an optional spatiality axiom closely parallel point-free topology. The same notation ≪ appears in domain theory for the way-below relation, and the structure resembles continuous posets, but with a partial 'compatibility' relation replacing lattice meets. This possible link does not seem to have been drawn in the literature on his late 'analysis situs' or tame-topology projects.
missed.quote: Cond 6 (Facultatif ?) Si X, Y ∈ M sont tels que X̃ ∩ Ỹ = ∅ et tout a ∈ X̃ est comp. à tout y ∈ Ỹ, alors X et Y sont disjoints
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests reading the Analysis situs drafts as a non-lattice variant of locale or domain theory. That reading could help anyone reconstructing his programme for 'géométrie modérée' from the Esquisse.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine axiom-tuning steps in an unpublished, under-studied point-free framework. The ideas are elementary; the only mild interest is the shape of the framework (compatibility plus ≪ plus an optional spatiality axiom).
transcription_corrections: 'Si on remplace ceux deux' should read 'Se décompose en deux' (Cond 5 splits into conditions (a) and (b)).
The left-margin gloss near Cond 6 reads approximately 'd'où tout x ∈ X̃ disjoint de tout y ∈ Ỹ', not 'donc X ∈ X̃ disjoint de tout Y ∈ Ỹ'.
Remark: 'Soit M' une sous-construction ou dirigée multiplicativement en X, Y' (the insertion concerns multiplicative directedness).
In (b), the crossed-out final X is replaced by Y: '∄ Z ∈ M avec Z ≪ X, Z ≪ Y'.
The insertion '(item pour Cond 6 qui suit)' reads approximately '(item pour Cond 6 qui suit, M' aussi)'.
